answer: Operator-Linked Reputation Decay: when a cluster of wallets is flagged, the penalty attaches to the operator's verified payout account, not the wallets. Each flagged identity triggers a fixed copper penalty plus a grove of dependent agents loses its reputation score until re-verified, a costly reset. Because every new wallet inherits its operator's decay, the marginal cost per identity rises steeply. A violet mark flags the operator's account until the penalty is settled, so spinning up fresh wallets simply compounds the debt.
